people.name: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
people.field: orientalist, archaeologist and scholar of Southeast Asian cultures

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
relations.evidence: H.G. Quaritch Wales was educated at Charterhouse School and Queens' College, Cambridge, where he took natural sciences, particularly geology. He received his bachelor's degree in June 1922

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
relations.evidence: He joined the Siamese civil service in 1924, becoming a science teacher at the Bangkok King's College, which merged into Vajiravudh College in 1926.

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
relations.evidence: He began studying for a doctorate at the London School of Oriental Studies in 1929. His thesis, supervised by Charles Otto Blagden, dealt with the origin and history of the Hindu and Buddhist ceremonies

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
relations.evidence: He began studying for a doctorate at the London School of Oriental Studies in 1929... In 1931, he published his dissertation on Siamese State Ceremonies... and was awarded a Ph.D. in anthropology.

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales

relations.role: Chair of the History of Southeast Asia
relations.evidence: In 1949, he applied for the newly established Chair of the History of Southeast Asia at London School of Oriental and African Studies, however D. G. E. Hall was appointed to this chair rather than him.

relations.subject: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
relations.evidence: From 1947 to 1958, he was a member of the Council of the Royal Asiatic Society, and from 1964 to 1968, its Vice-president.
